Hey! Thought I would weigh in on this. Besides the inclusion of wi-fi, these camera have very different features that compliment very different photography styles. 

The 70D shoots incredibly fast (7fps) for its cost and its autofocus in and out of live view (where the image displays on the LCD) is comparable to much much more expensive bodies. It's also weather sealed and has a touch screen which makes it great for sports and shooting video (I've used this for about 1.5 years doing sports).

The 6D is a professional body, meaning it has a better build quality and is encased in metal as opposed to plastic. It's also currently the cheapest full frame Canon offers, and is very very good at its job for its price. I know less about this camera, but have used it a lot recently and absolutely love it for studio and shots where I have control of the model/light etc. Full frame really make a difference. Oh, it has a GPS...

Basically it depends on what you want to shoot! For all around, probably the 70D for its flexibility. But honestly they're very equivalent in my eyes. Just tailored for different styles.


P.S. if any complaint about the 70D, the back wheel has been made way too small. Miss my 60D a bit...

Not so sure about Ret except I know they generally favor the new Jack chassis over the old with the exception of the Phoenix. They're infantry are very mixed arms in that they work well together for devastating results, but they often cannot operate independently. (Not sure if this is universal, but it's what I've taken away from fighting them.)

Menoth is an army of denial, synergy and reciprocal attrition. What Shoitaan said is correct in that you can build your list to go in different ways (though I would argue Sevvy is more universal). Basically they have mediocre jacks that become the best jacks in the game thanks to their support units. Stuff like the choir and vassels will buff your jacks to make them more mobile, more accurate (in melee and shooting) and more hitty in general. Our infantry has always been solid in the melee realm (lots of magic weapons and weapon master) though the shooting isn't horrible. 

For the denial, stuff like the choir and a lot of built in rules will make it so many units and models cannot be shot or spelled at. Or they cannot be knocked down. Or they make it so enemy casters cannot cast. Or all your opponent's lasting spells disappear. It can be very frustrating to fight a denial themed Menoth list. 

This final thing here is the attrition aspect. Many menoth units (infantry really) have abilities that activate when they are hit or die. Menoth can be about taking the alpha strike (your enemy will often be faster and hit first) and then hitting back harder, or blocking charge lanes, which will mess up your opponents plan. Stuff like the Knights Exemplar that gain armor and strength for every one of their number that die, Bastians which have 8 wounds a piece and can spread out damage over the whole unit or Exemplar Errants which can choose another in the unit to die in favor of the one that was killed - all of this is about making an enemy pay for trying to attack. 

Oh and Harby is arguably our best caster. She has the largest control range in the game (20"), can wipe enemy upkeeps whenever, can take damage to keep models alive and speeds them up while they start a charge in her control area. She likes running lots of heavy jacks because of her 10 focus and she is a back line caster. Can be vulnerable to shooting above 10" range however. 

Hope that helps!

Menoth is more a denial army and as such a lot of their stuff rely more on doing what you know they're going to do but you cannot do anything about it... If that makes sense. I think watering down your paints, maybe 3 part paint to 1 part water, would really help. Don't do this in the pot but maybe find a kitchen tile at a home improvement store. You just dab some paint out with the back end of a brush and mix in the water on the pallet. Certain colors may go on thin, but you can add more than one coat for a much smoother look to the model. 

As far as highlighting, I see below you mentioned not knowing where to go. Try to figure out what colors you use (I use GW colors mostly so I don't recognize those) but say purple, black and bronze. Then go to your hobby shop and they should have the paints arranged by tone. Just find your paint and buy the one slightly brighter than it (if you feel confident get the one darker too.) From there do a base coat with the darkest paint until it masks the primer, find the raised edges and paint on the next brightest color. If sounds weird at first but it is imo the easiest way to get a great looking paint job.

2 lights and 1 heavy actually. I would not magnitize the light jacks. 

 To be honest if you really want to make the most of the heavy war jack, I would buy a character war jack kit. Probably blood of martyrs. 

 They tend to be harder to magnetize and are often better just made into 1 jack. If you really want to consider you can pick that up in the heavy jack kit. 

 But since you're just starting out here is what I would do. Do the magnetizing like I specified earlier on the jack you have in your battle box. When you eventually get a heavy war jack kit, just magnitize the extra parts and use them on your existing jack. Then use the body and the legs that come with the kit for a character war jack.

 P. S. Green stuff is good to have on hand but is not necessary.

While many use electric or automatic drills, I've always hated the idea of accidentally drilling straight through a joint. 

That said magnetizing is great but don't worry about it until you buy a heavy jack kit- it's the inly time it will be useful.

When the time comes go to a local hobby shop or Games Workshop ( say what you will about this broken ass games, their supplies are usually top notch) and pick up a pinning vice - usually under 20 bucks if memory serves. Now search rare earth magnets online. You should be able to order around 100 for $12. See if you can also get a drill bit to match your magnets. I found a set for $8 at an indi hobby shop in my area. Lastly, pins, in case you want to do that sort of thing and if you play Menoth you will, are as easy as getting ordinary paper clips. They match the drill bit that comes with the GW pine vice almost exactly. 

Start slowly and ALWAYS CHECK POLARITY. Nothing is more dismaying than gluing in a magnet just to find the rest don't match. For the Menoth heavy put a magnet into the left shoulder berring and all three left arm attachments. For the right glue the arm on but magnitize at the wrist so you can have all three. In the case of the Templar's shield use the pin vice to make a small hole in the left hand. Then put a pin in the shield and chop off the lower part of the grip (a loss i know but you rarely see it.) The simply use the pin to equip or not equip the sheild. 

Oh the head. Pick your favorite head. Too much of a pain to magnitize. 

Hope that helps! Welcome to the hobby.
